points.t: Any dry or eczematous skin, at every review, alongside active treatment.
Emollients replace lipids and water in the stratum corneum, restore the barrier and reduce itch and flares.
The right emollient is the one the patient will use: generous quantities (children 250–500 g a week), used as a soap substitute too; stop aqueous cream as a leave-on.
Fire risk with all emollients soaking into fabrics (MHRA); slips on bath additives; stinging from preservatives or aqueous cream.

points: **Quantity check:** NICE CG57 — **250–500 g/week** for children; about **500 g/week** for adults with widespread dryness. A patient collecting one 500 g tub every 3 months is under-using.
Prescribe enough for **home and nursery/school** (NICE CG57).

items.t: Warn about **fire risk**: dressings, clothing and bedding soaked in any emollient (paraffin or paraffin-free) can catch fire easily (MHRA).

pearls.t: "Emollients are the treatment, not an extra."
Show the FTU *and* a handful of emollient. For a child with widespread eczema, a 500 g tub should last about a week.
Fire-safety counselling is an MHRA expectation — record that you gave it.
